// ===== codec.d.ts =====
import { CompressionType } from './packet.js';
/**
 * A compression algorithm implementation.
 *
 * ONE registry serves both directions, so the API can never end up
 * asymmetric (able to decompress an algorithm it cannot compress, or vice
 * versa). `limit` bounds the OUTPUT size: `decompress` must stop and throw
 * as soon as the produced bytes exceed it — never inflate fully and check
 * afterwards, which is exactly how a decompression bomb wins.
 */
export interface CompressionCodec {
    readonly type: CompressionType;
    compress(input: Uint8Array, limit: number): Promise<Uint8Array>;
    decompress(input: Uint8Array, limit: number): Promise<Uint8Array>;
}
export declare class CodecRegistry {
    private readonly codecs;
    constructor(codecs?: readonly CompressionCodec[]);
    register(codec: CompressionCodec): void;
    get(type: CompressionType): CompressionCodec | undefined;
    /** The codec, or throw — used by send/receive paths that must not proceed. */
    require(type: CompressionType): CompressionCodec;
}
/**
 * Zlib (RFC 1950) via the platform's native `CompressionStream` /
 * `DecompressionStream('deflate')` — the Web Streams `'deflate'` format IS
 * zlib (deflate with the zlib wrapper), matching Rust's `flate2` Zlib codec.
 * Available in all modern browsers and Node ≥ 18; no wasm, no dependency.
 */
export declare class ZlibCodec implements CompressionCodec {
    readonly type: 2;
    compress(input: Uint8Array, limit: number): Promise<Uint8Array>;
    decompress(input: Uint8Array, limit: number): Promise<Uint8Array>;
}
//# sourceMappingURL=codec.d.ts.map
// ===== constants.d.ts =====
export declare const PROTOCOL_VERSION = 1;
export declare const FIXED_HEADER_LEN = 16;
/** Wire-format ceiling for `ext_header_len` — the field is a u16. */
export declare const WIRE_MAX_EXT_HEADER_LEN = 65535;
/** Wire-format ceiling for `payload_len` — the field is a u32. */
export declare const WIRE_MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN = 4294967295;
/**
 * Default maximum decoded payload per frame: 16 MiB.
 *
 * Mirrors the Rust 2.0 `DecodeLimits` default (the decompression-bomb cap),
 * enforced there identically by TCP / WebSocket / QUIC. The old TS default
 * was the raw wire ceiling (4 GiB), so this client could happily encode a
 * frame the server was guaranteed to kill the connection over.
 */
export declare const DEFAULT_MAX_PAYLOAD_LEN: number;
/** Default maximum ext-header per frame: the u16 wire ceiling. */
export declare const DEFAULT_MAX_EXT_HEADER_LEN = 65535;
//# sourceMappingURL=constants.d.ts.map
// ===== errors.d.ts =====
export declare class WireFormatError extends Error {
    constructor(message: string);
}
export declare class UnsupportedVersionError extends WireFormatError {
    readonly version: number;
    constructor(version: number);
}
export declare class IncompletePacketError extends WireFormatError {
    constructor(message: string);
}
/**
 * An unknown wire byte where an enum is expected (packet type, compression).
 *
 * Mirrors Rust 2.0's `TryFrom<u8>` decode: an unrecognized value is a protocol
 * error, never silently accepted as a bogus enum member the way the old
 * unchecked `as PacketType` cast did.
 */
export declare class UnknownWireValueError extends WireFormatError {
    readonly field: string;
    readonly value: number;
    constructor(field: string, value: number);
}
/**
 * A structurally valid frame that exceeds the configured `DecodeLimits`
 * (payload, ext header, or decompressed size). A protocol-level violation:
 * under strict semantics the connection is closed, matching the Rust side.
 */
export declare class DecodeLimitError extends WireFormatError {
    constructor(message: string);
}
export declare class TransportError extends Error {
    constructor(message: string);
}
/**
 * Thrown by `send()` when the packet would push the WebSocket's outbound
 * buffer (`bufferedAmount` + this frame) over the configured high-water mark.
 * The socket is NOT closed — the connection stays healthy; the caller should
 * back off (drop, queue, or retry later) instead of piling more bytes onto a
 * link that isn't draining.
 */
export declare class BackpressureError extends TransportError {
    /** Bytes currently sitting in the socket's outbound buffer. */
    readonly bufferedAmount: number;
    /** The high-water mark that would be exceeded. */
    readonly maxBufferedBytes: number;
    constructor(bufferedAmount: number, maxBufferedBytes: number);
}
/**
 * No codec is available for the requested compression algorithm.
 *
 * On SEND this rejects the call — a raw payload is never shipped under a
 * compressed header. On RECEIVE it is fatal: the peer is speaking an algorithm
 * this client cannot undo, so the connection is closed rather than handing the
 * application compressed bytes it would mistake for plaintext.
 */
export declare class UnsupportedCompressionError extends WireFormatError {
    readonly compression: number;
    constructor(compression: number);
}
/**
 * The per-connection message-id counter reached the u32 ceiling.
 *
 * Ids never repeat within a connection generation (responses are matched on
 * the bare u32, so a wrapped id could complete someone else's request — the
 * ABA the Rust 2.0 registry closed). A reconnect starts a fresh generation
 * with a fresh counter.
 */
export declare class IdExhaustedError extends TransportError {
    constructor();
}
export declare class RequestTimeoutError extends Error {
    readonly messageId: number;
    readonly timeoutMs: number;
    constructor(messageId: number, timeoutMs: number);
}

// ===== heartbeat.d.ts =====
import type { TransportClient } from './transport-client.js';
/**
 * Application-layer heartbeat.
 *
 * msgtrans has NO protocol-level ping — a liveness probe is application
 * traffic by design (the wire stays payload-agnostic). This monitor owns the
 * scheduling and the verdict; the caller supplies the probe: any
 * request/response the peer is obliged to answer.
 */
export interface HeartbeatOptions {
    /**
     * The liveness probe. Called when the connection has been idle for
     * `intervalMs`; resolving counts as proof of life, rejecting (or exceeding
     * `timeoutMs`) declares the connection dead. Typically a cheap
     * request/response, e.g. `() => client.request(pingBytes, { timeoutMs })`.
     */
    probe: () => Promise<unknown>;
    /** Idle time before a probe fires. Default 30_000. */
    intervalMs?: number;
    /** Probe deadline. Default 10_000. */
    timeoutMs?: number;
    /**
     * Called when the probe fails — the connection is presumed dead. Default:
     * `client.close()`, which lets a reconnect manager (or the app's own
     * close handling) take over. The monitor never reconnects by itself:
     * detection and recovery are separate jobs.
     */
    onDead?: (error: unknown) => void;
}
/**
 * Idle-based heartbeat: traffic in EITHER direction counts as activity, so a
 * busy connection is never probed — the probe exists to disambiguate
 * "quiet because idle" from "quiet because dead", and only the former needs
 * disambiguating.
 */
export declare class HeartbeatMonitor {
    private readonly client;
    private readonly probe;
    private readonly intervalMs;
    private readonly timeoutMs;
    private readonly onDead;
    private lastActivity;
    private timer;
    private probing;
    private readonly unsubscribes;
    /**
     * Bumped by every stop(): an in-flight probe belongs to the epoch it was
     * launched in, and a verdict from a dead epoch is VOID — the old behavior
     * let a stale probe failure close whatever connection came next.
     */
    private epoch;
    constructor(client: TransportClient, options: HeartbeatOptions);
    get isRunning(): boolean;
    start(): void;
    stop(): void;
    private tick;
}

// ===== packet.d.ts =====
export declare const PacketType: {
    readonly OneWay: 0;
    readonly Request: 1;
    readonly Response: 2;
};
export type PacketType = (typeof PacketType)[keyof typeof PacketType];
export declare const CompressionType: {
    readonly None: 0;
    readonly Zstd: 1;
    readonly Zlib: 2;
};
export type CompressionType = (typeof CompressionType)[keyof typeof CompressionType];
/**
 * Wire metadata bits in the `reserved` field.
 *
 * `HighPriority` and `HasRouteTag` are annotations a peer may read.
 * `Fragmented` describes a mechanism this client does not implement —
 * `WebSocketTransport.send()` refuses to send it rather than shipping a
 * promise the receiver cannot rely on.
 */
export declare const ReservedFlag: {
    readonly Fragmented: 1;
    readonly HighPriority: 2;
    readonly HasRouteTag: 4;
};
/**
 * Frame-decoding caps, mirroring Rust 2.0's `DecodeLimits`.
 *
 * The frame cap is DERIVED (header + ext + payload), never set independently:
 * a max frame that disagreed with its parts would reject frames whose parts
 * were each individually legal. The default payload cap matches the Rust
 * decompression-bomb cap (16 MiB), so both peers agree on what fits.
 */
export interface DecodeLimits {
    readonly maxPayloadLen: number;
    readonly maxExtHeaderLen: number;
}
export declare const DEFAULT_DECODE_LIMITS: DecodeLimits;
/**
 * Validate caller-supplied limits and clamp them into what the wire format
 * can express. VALIDATE, not coerce: `NaN` makes every `>` comparison false,
 * which silently disables the decompression-bomb defense — an invalid limit
 * is a thrown error, never a quietly-open door.
 */
export declare function normalizeDecodeLimits(limits?: Partial<DecodeLimits>): DecodeLimits;
export interface PacketInit {
    packetType: PacketType;
    messageId: number;
    bizType?: number;
    compression?: CompressionType;
    extHeader?: Uint8Array;
    payload?: Uint8Array;
    reserved?: number;
    version?: number;
}
export declare class Packet {
    version: number;
    compression: CompressionType;
    packetType: PacketType;
    bizType: number;
    messageId: number;
    reserved: number;
    extHeader: Uint8Array;
    payload: Uint8Array;
    constructor(init: PacketInit);
    static oneWay(messageId: number, payload?: Uint8Array): Packet;
    static request(messageId: number, payload?: Uint8Array): Packet;
    static response(messageId: number, payload?: Uint8Array): Packet;
    hasFlag(flag: number): boolean;
    setFlag(flag: number, on?: boolean): void;
    totalLength(): number;
    /**
     * Encode to wire bytes.
     *
     * Enforces the SAME caps the peer decodes with: without `limits` the
     * defaults apply, so this client cannot produce a frame a default-configured
     * Rust 2.0 server is guaranteed to close the connection over. (The old
     * behavior checked only the raw u16/u32 wire ceilings — up to 4 GiB.)
     */
    encode(limits?: DecodeLimits): Uint8Array;
    /**
     * STRICT decode of exactly one packet.
     *
     * One WebSocket binary message carries exactly one packet, so this is the
     * only decode shape: trailing bytes mean the stream is desynchronized and
     * are a protocol error, not tolerated silence. Unknown packet-type or
     * compression bytes are protocol errors (`UnknownWireValueError`) instead
     * of being cast into bogus enum members. Declared lengths over the
     * configured `DecodeLimits` are rejected before any allocation.
     */
    static decodeExact(bytes: Uint8Array, limits?: DecodeLimits): Packet;
}
//# sourceMappingURL=packet.d.ts.map
// ===== reconnect.d.ts =====
import type { TransportClient } from './transport-client.js';
export type ReconnectPhase = 'reconnecting' | 'connected' | 'gave-up';
export interface ReconnectOptions {
    /** Delay before the first reconnect attempt. Default 1_000. */
    initialDelayMs?: number;
    /** Backoff cap. Default 30_000. */
    maxDelayMs?: number;
    /** Per-attempt multiplier. Default 2. */
    multiplier?: number;
    /** Give up after this many consecutive failures. Default Infinity. */
    maxAttempts?: number;
    /**
     * Backoff jitter, 0..1. Each delay is multiplied by
     * `1 - jitterRatio * random()`, spreading a fleet's reconnects instead of
     * synchronizing a thundering herd on the same schedule. Default 0.2;
     * 0 disables (deterministic delays, e.g. for tests).
     */
    jitterRatio?: number;
    /** Observability hook; `attempt` is 1-based within the current outage. */
    onStateChange?: (phase: ReconnectPhase, attempt: number) => void;
}
/**
 * Automatic reconnection with exponential backoff.
 *
 * Contract, stated bluntly because every reconnect bug in this project has
 * been a contract ambiguity:
 *
 * - While the handle is ACTIVE, every `close` event triggers a reconnect
 *   cycle. An intentional disconnect must call `stop()` FIRST — the
 *   transport cannot tell a wanted close from an unwanted one.
 * - One cycle runs at a time; a `close` arriving mid-cycle is absorbed
 *   (the cycle is already doing the right thing).
 * - Backoff resets after a successful `connect()`, and the pending requests
 *   of the old connection are NOT replayed — the transport rejected them at
 *   close (pending state rides the connection); replay policy belongs to
 *   the application layer, which knows what is idempotent.
 * - `stop()` during a backoff sleep abandons the cycle at the next wake.
 * - This is THE retry policy. `TransportClientOptions.connectRetry` defaults
 *   to zero retries; leave it there when using this manager — stacking both
 *   multiplies attempt counts and wait times.
 */
export declare class ReconnectManager {
    private readonly client;
    private readonly opts;
    /** A close observed while a cycle was running: re-examined when it ends. */
    private pendingRerun;
    private readonly onStateChange;
    private active;
    private cycleRunning;
    private unsubscribe;
    constructor(client: TransportClient, options?: ReconnectOptions);
    get isActive(): boolean;
    start(): void;
    stop(): void;
    private runCycle;
    private jittered;
}
//# sourceMappingURL=reconnect.d.ts.map
// ===== transport-client.d.ts =====
import { CompressionType, type DecodeLimits, Packet } from './packet.js';
import { type CompressionCodec } from './codec.js';
import type { EnqueuedInfo, Transport } from './transport.js';
import { type TextFramePolicy, type WebSocketFactory } from './websocket-transport.js';
export interface SendOptions {
    bizType?: number;
    extHeader?: Uint8Array;
    /**
     * Compression algorithm. The registered codec is applied on THIS side
     * before enqueue; if no codec is registered for the algorithm the send
     * rejects — a raw payload is never shipped under a compressed header.
     * `ZlibCodec` is registered by default; Zstd is injectable via
     * `TransportClientOptions.codecs`.
     */
    compression?: CompressionType;
}
export interface RequestOptions extends SendOptions {
    /** Override the default request timeout. Pass 0 to disable. */
    timeoutMs?: number;
}
export interface TransportClientOptions {
    url?: string;
    transport?: 'websocket' | Transport;
    protocols?: string | string[];
    webSocketFactory?: WebSocketFactory;
    onTextFrame?: TextFramePolicy;
    /** Outbound-buffer high-water mark; see
     *  `WebSocketTransportOptions.maxBufferedBytes`. */
    maxBufferedBytes?: number;
    defaultTimeoutMs?: number;
    /**
     * Frame caps, enforced in both directions (default: 16 MiB payload /
     * 65535 ext header — the Rust 2.0 defaults, so both peers agree on what
     * fits). Also bounds decompressed size.
     */
    limits?: Partial<DecodeLimits>;
    /**
     * Inbound normalization queue caps (packets queued behind an in-flight
     * decompression). Overflow closes the connection: the browser cannot
     * pause the socket, but it can refuse to buffer without limit.
     * Defaults: 8192 frames / 64 MiB.
     */
    maxInboundQueueFrames?: number;
    maxInboundQueueBytes?: number;
    /**
     * Outbound chain cap (sends queued behind an in-flight compression).
     * Exceeding it rejects the send with `BackpressureError` — the
     * connection stays healthy. Default 8192.
     */
    maxOutboundQueue?: number;
    /**
     * Additional compression codecs. `ZlibCodec` (native
     * Compression/DecompressionStream) is always registered; entries here can
     * add Zstd or override the built-in.
     */
    codecs?: readonly CompressionCodec[];
    /**
     * Connect-time retry policy. Default: no retry (one attempt only).
     *
     * This is the language mapping of the Rust crate's `RetryConfig`. It
     * covers the *initial* `connect()` failure path — DNS / WebSocket
     * handshake / cold-start network blips — not auto-reconnect after a
     * dropped connection, which is the consuming SDK's responsibility
     * (`@privchat/sdk` runs its own `ReconnectOptions` state machine on
     * top of this transport).
     *
     * Default 0 retries preserves the original single-attempt behavior.
     * Opt in by passing `{ maxRetries: N, ... }`.
     */
    connectRetry?: ConnectRetryOptions;
}
/**
 * Connect-time retry policy. Mirrors Rust `msgtrans` `RetryConfig`.
 *
 *   - `maxRetries`: number of ADDITIONAL attempts after the first one
 *     fails. Total attempts = `maxRetries + 1`. Default 0 (no retry).
 *   - `initialDelayMs`: delay before the FIRST retry (i.e. after attempt #0
 *     fails, before attempt #1). Default 100.
 *   - `maxDelayMs`: cap applied after exponential growth. Default 10_000.
 *   - `multiplier`: per-attempt backoff multiplier. Default 2.
 *
 * Delay formula for attempt `n` (1-indexed retry): `min(maxDelayMs,
 * initialDelayMs * multiplier^(n - 1))`.
 *
 * Retry is unconditional — any `transport.connect()` rejection triggers
 * a retry until `maxRetries` is exhausted. The last error is rethrown.
 */
export interface ConnectRetryOptions {
    maxRetries?: number;
    initialDelayMs?: number;
    maxDelayMs?: number;
    multiplier?: number;
}
export declare class TransportClient {
    private readonly transport;
    private readonly requestManager;
    private readonly limits;
    private readonly codecs;
    private normalizer;
    private readonly inboundCaps;
    private readonly maxOutboundQueue;
    private readonly messageListeners;
    private readonly requestListeners;
    private readonly messageEnqueuedListeners;
    private readonly closeListeners;
    private readonly errorListeners;
    private readonly retryOpts;
    /**
     * Program-order guarantee for the outbound path. Compression is async, so
     * without serialization `send(a, {compression}); send(b);` would put `b`
     * on the wire first — the outbound mirror of the inbound reordering the
     * normalizer chain prevents. Every outbound packet passes through this
     * chain; a plain send behind a compressing one waits for it, exactly as
     * Rust's inline `SendOptions::apply` on the send path.
     */
    private outboundChain;
    /** Outbound packets queued or in flight on the chain. */
    private outboundDepth;
    /**
     * Connection generation, bumped on every close. A `ClientRequest` captures
     * the generation it arrived on; its `respond()` refuses to write onto a
     * LATER connection — the client-side mapping of Rust 2.0's
     * generation-bound respond claims.
     */
    private generation;
    constructor(options: TransportClientOptions);
    /**
     * Open the transport with optional retry-on-failure.
     *
     * Attempt 0 runs immediately. If it rejects and `connectRetry.maxRetries
     * > 0`, the transport is `close()`d (defensively, to reset any
     * mid-Connecting state that would otherwise cause subsequent
     * `transport.connect()` calls to return the prior rejected promise),
     * a backoff delay is applied, and another attempt is made — up to
     * `maxRetries` additional times. The final attempt's rejection is
     * thrown verbatim.
     */
    connect(): Promise<void>;
    /** Close the underlying transport. Alias: `disconnect()`. */
    close(): Promise<void>;
    /** Alias for `close()` — matches Rust `TransportClient::disconnect()`. */
    disconnect(): Promise<void>;
    isConnected(): boolean;
    /**
     * One-way send. Resolves when the packet was ACCEPTED by the socket's
     * outbound buffer (enqueue-confirmed — a browser WebSocket offers no
     * write confirmation, and this API does not pretend otherwise).
     */
    send(payload: Uint8Array, options?: SendOptions): Promise<void>;
    request(payload: Uint8Array, options?: RequestOptions): Promise<Uint8Array>;
    /** Respond path, reachable only through the closure handed to
     *  `ClientRequest` at construction. */
    private respondTo;
    on(event: 'message', cb: (msg: ClientMessage) => void): () => void;
    on(event: 'request', cb: (req: ClientRequest) => void): () => void;
    on(event: 'messageEnqueued', cb: (info: EnqueuedInfo) => void): () => void;
    on(event: 'close', cb: (event?: unknown) => void): () => void;
    on(event: 'error', cb: (error: unknown) => void): () => void;
    private handleIncoming;
    private route;
    private buildOutbound;
    /** Sync bypass is safe only when there is no codec work AND nothing is
     *  queued on the chain (otherwise this packet would overtake it). */
    private canBypassChain;
    /** Synchronous packet construction for the no-compression path. */
    private buildPlain;
    private scheduleOutbound;
    private dispatchMessageEnqueued;
    private dispatchClose;
    private dispatchError;
}
/** A one-way message delivered to the application. Always plaintext: the
 *  inbound normalizer has already undone any compression. */
export declare class ClientMessage {
    private readonly packet;
    /** @internal — constructed by the transport only. */
    constructor(token: unknown, packet: Packet);
    get payload(): Uint8Array;
    /** Alias for `payload`. */
    get data(): Uint8Array;
    get bizType(): number;
    get messageId(): number;
    get extHeader(): Uint8Array;
}
/**
 * A request delivered to the client that carries the obligation to answer —
 * the TS mapping of Rust 2.0's `ClientRequest`. `respond()` answers it at
 * most once (runtime-enforced; TS cannot consume ownership at the type
 * level), and only onto the connection generation it arrived on: a stale
 * response written after a reconnect could complete a DIFFERENT server-side
 * request that drew the same id.
 */
interface RespondPath {
    isCurrent: () => boolean;
    respond: (request: ClientRequest, payload: Uint8Array, options: SendOptions) => Promise<void>;
}
export declare class ClientRequest {
    private respondedFlag;
    private readonly packet;
    private readonly path;
    /** @internal — constructed by the transport only. An externally
     *  constructible ClientRequest could respond with an arbitrary messageId,
     *  which is exactly the forgeable handle this type exists to prevent. */
    constructor(token: unknown, packet: Packet, path: RespondPath);
    /** @internal */
    stillCurrent(): boolean;
    get payload(): Uint8Array;
    /** Alias for `payload`. */
    get data(): Uint8Array;
    get bizType(): number;
    get messageId(): number;
    get extHeader(): Uint8Array;
    get hasResponded(): boolean;
    respond(payload: Uint8Array, options?: SendOptions): Promise<void>;
}
export {};
//# sourceMappingURL=transport-client.d.ts.map
// ===== transport.d.ts =====
import type { Packet } from './packet.js';
export declare const TransportState: {
    readonly Idle: "idle";
    readonly Connecting: "connecting";
    readonly Open: "open";
    readonly Closing: "closing";
    readonly Closed: "closed";
};
export type TransportState = (typeof TransportState)[keyof typeof TransportState];
/**
 * Emitted when a packet has been ACCEPTED by the underlying socket's outbound
 * buffer. Deliberately named "enqueued", not "sent": a browser WebSocket
 * offers no write completion, so nothing at this layer can prove the bytes
 * reached the network. (Rust 2.0's `send` is write-confirmed; this tier is
 * the honest browser equivalent, and pretending otherwise would recreate the
 * fake write confirmations 2.0 was built to kill.)
 */
export interface EnqueuedInfo {
    messageId: number;
}
export interface Transport {
    connect(): Promise<void>;
    send(packet: Packet): Promise<void>;
    close(): Promise<void>;
    isConnected(): boolean;
    onMessage(cb: (packet: Packet) => void): void;
    onMessageEnqueued(cb: (info: EnqueuedInfo) => void): void;
    onClose(cb: (event?: unknown) => void): void;
    onError(cb: (error: unknown) => void): void;
}
//# sourceMappingURL=transport.d.ts.map
// ===== websocket-transport.d.ts =====
import { type DecodeLimits, Packet } from './packet.js';
import { type EnqueuedInfo, type Transport, TransportState } from './transport.js';
export interface WebSocketLike {
    binaryType: string;
    readyState: number;
    /** Bytes queued via send() but not yet flushed to the network.
     *  Standard on browser/`ws` WebSockets; optional here so minimal
     *  fakes keep working (absence disables the backpressure check). */
    bufferedAmount?: number;
    send(data: ArrayBufferLike | ArrayBufferView | string): void;
    close(code?: number, reason?: string): void;
    onopen: ((ev: unknown) => void) | null;
    onmessage: ((ev: {
        data: unknown;
    }) => void) | null;
    onerror: ((ev: unknown) => void) | null;
    onclose: ((ev: unknown) => void) | null;
}
export type WebSocketFactory = (url: string, protocols?: string | string[]) => WebSocketLike;
export type TextFramePolicy = 'error' | 'ignore';
export interface WebSocketTransportOptions {
    url: string;
    protocols?: string | string[];
    /**
     * Override the WebSocket constructor. Defaults to `globalThis.WebSocket`.
     * Use this to inject `ws` in Node, or a mock in tests.
     */
    webSocketFactory?: WebSocketFactory;
    /**
     * What to do with WebSocket text frames. msgtrans canonical traffic is
     * Binary-only (see WIRE_FORMAT.md §9.1); a text frame is non-protocol
     * traffic. Default `'error'`: report and CLOSE the connection (strict,
     * matching Rust 2.0's frame policy — a desynchronized peer is not
     * trustworthy). `'ignore'` drops them silently.
     */
    onTextFrame?: TextFramePolicy;
    /**
     * Outbound-buffer high-water mark in bytes. `send()` rejects with
     * `BackpressureError` when the socket's `bufferedAmount` PLUS this frame
     * would exceed the mark — the projection matters: checking only the
     * current level let a 10 MiB frame sail through at 15.9/16 MiB. The
     * connection itself is left open. Default 16 MiB; `0` disables the check.
     * Sockets that don't report `bufferedAmount` are never rejected.
     */
    maxBufferedBytes?: number;
    /**
     * Frame-decoding caps, enforced in BOTH directions with the same numbers
     * (mirroring Rust 2.0, where one `DecodeLimits` serves every protocol):
     * inbound frames over the caps close the connection; outbound frames over
     * the caps are rejected here instead of letting the server kill the
     * connection over them. Defaults match the Rust defaults.
     */
    limits?: Partial<DecodeLimits>;
}
/** Default outbound high-water mark: 16 MiB. */
export declare const DEFAULT_MAX_BUFFERED_BYTES: number;
export declare class WebSocketTransport implements Transport {
    private readonly opts;
    private readonly limits;
    private ws;
    private _state;
    private readonly messageHandlers;
    private readonly messageEnqueuedHandlers;
    private readonly closeHandlers;
    private readonly errorHandlers;
    private connectPromise;
    private connectResolve;
    private connectReject;
    constructor(opts: WebSocketTransportOptions);
    get state(): TransportState;
    isConnected(): boolean;
    connect(): Promise<void>;
    send(packet: Packet): Promise<void>;
    close(): Promise<void>;
    onMessage(cb: (packet: Packet) => void): void;
    onMessageEnqueued(cb: (info: EnqueuedInfo) => void): void;
    onClose(cb: (event?: unknown) => void): void;
    onError(cb: (error: unknown) => void): void;
    private handleMessage;
    private decodeAndDispatch;
    /** Report a protocol violation and close: strict framing has no
     *  keep-going path. */
    private fatal;
    private handleError;
    private handleClose;
    private dispatchError;
}
//# sourceMappingURL=websocket-transport.d.ts.map
// ===== webtransport-transport.d.ts =====
import { type DecodeLimits, Packet } from './packet.js';
import { type EnqueuedInfo, type Transport, TransportState } from './transport.js';
/**
 * The subset of the WebTransport API this adapter needs — injectable so
 * tests (and non-browser hosts) can supply a fake.
 */
export interface WebTransportLike {
    readonly ready: Promise<void>;
    readonly closed: Promise<unknown>;
    close(closeInfo?: {
        closeCode?: number;
        reason?: string;
    }): void;
    createBidirectionalStream(): Promise<{
        readable: ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
        writable: WritableStream<Uint8Array>;
    }>;
}
export type WebTransportFactory = (url: string) => WebTransportLike;
export interface WebTransportTransportOptions {
    /** https:// URL of the WebTransport endpoint. */
    url: string;
    /** Override the WebTransport constructor. Defaults to
     *  `globalThis.WebTransport`. */
    webTransportFactory?: WebTransportFactory;
    /** Frame caps, both directions; defaults mirror the Rust 2.0 defaults. */
    limits?: Partial<DecodeLimits>;
}
/**
 * msgtrans over WebTransport (HTTP/3).
 *
 * Framing mirrors the Rust QUIC adapter so the two can interoperate the day
 * a server exposes a WebTransport endpoint: ONE bidirectional stream per
 * connection, each msgtrans frame preceded by a 4-byte big-endian length.
 * The stream is a byte stream (unlike WebSocket's message framing), so this
 * adapter owns reassembly: partial prefixes, partial frames and multiple
 * frames per chunk are all normal.
 *
 * Semantics match the WebSocket adapter exactly:
 * - `send()` resolves when the chunk was ACCEPTED by the stream writer
 *   (enqueue-confirmed; the writer's promise is the platform's own
 *   backpressure, so no separate high-water mark is layered on top).
 * - Strict inbound: an over-limit length prefix or an undecodable frame
 *   closes the connection.
 * - `ReservedFlag.Fragmented` is refused (nothing implements reassembly).
 * - Generation isolation: a previous session's late readable/closed events
 *   cannot act on the replacement connection.
 */
export declare class WebTransportTransport implements Transport {
    private readonly opts;
    private readonly limits;
    private session;
    private writer;
    private _state;
    private readonly messageHandlers;
    private readonly messageEnqueuedHandlers;
    private readonly closeHandlers;
    private readonly errorHandlers;
    constructor(opts: WebTransportTransportOptions);
    get state(): TransportState;
    isConnected(): boolean;
    connect(): Promise<void>;
    send(packet: Packet): Promise<void>;
    close(): Promise<void>;
    onMessage(cb: (packet: Packet) => void): void;
    onMessageEnqueued(cb: (info: EnqueuedInfo) => void): void;
    onClose(cb: (event?: unknown) => void): void;
    onError(cb: (error: unknown) => void): void;
    /**
     * Reassemble length-prefixed frames from the byte stream and dispatch
     * strictly decoded packets. Every protocol violation is fatal.
     */
    private readLoop;
    private fatal;
    private handleClose;
    private dispatchError;
}
//# sourceMappingURL=webtransport-transport.d.ts.map
